flows.period: Week ended Wed 2 Sep 2026 (LSEG Lipper / BofA-EPFR Flow Show) -- one full week newer than the prior 26-Aug baseline; the week-ended-9-Sep release is due today/tomorrow and not yet published.
flows.narrative: The week ended 2 Sep showed a classic flight-to-safety rotation: global money-market/cash funds drew +$46.1bn (Lipper), the largest weekly inflow in about a month, as US-Iran tension and a global bond selloff pushed investors toward cash. US equity funds saw a further -$11.12bn outflow (Lipper) / -$5.9bn (BofA-EPFR, a second straight week of outflows) even as Europe (+$13.09bn) and Asia (+$4.22bn) equity funds took in fresh money. EM equities show a genuine cross-provider discrepancy: Lipper's mutual-fund data shows an 8th consecutive weekly inflow (+$1.99bn) while BofA-EPFR's ETF-inclusive data shows outflows resumed (-$5.4bn) -- flagged rather than reconciled. Gold/precious-metals funds logged their 8th consecutive weekly inflow (+$2.85bn Lipper / +$3.2bn BofA), consistent with the miners complex's continued strength this week.
